name: Remotion cinematic renderer
observations: OpenMontage revision 195eab24478dc9363326aec437aefc3701635ddf contains a Remotion composition named CinematicRenderer, registered at 1920x1080 and 30 fps, plus a fixture composition SignalFromTomorrowWithMusic. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:153-176.

The renderer accepts a scenes array, optional title sizing and signal-line count, two independent audio tracks (soundtrack and music), and word-timed captions. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:1-67.

Video scenes support source resolution, tone, trim-before/after seconds, playback rate, CSS filter, and frame-bounded fade-in/fade-out. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:9-19; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:37-112.

Title scenes support multiline text, accent and intensity, optional background video with independent trims, and plate or transparent overlay variants. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:21-30; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:161-385.

Video scenes are rendered with OffthreadVideo, object-cover scaling, a default contrast/saturation/brightness filter, tone gradient, vignette, and edge treatment. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:74-110.

Title cards use a spring entrance, 3-frame word staggering, 14-frame word fade/blur/translate reveal, a 14-frame exit window, signal-texture scanlines, accent flares, and optional blurred background video. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:184-219, 230-382.

Soundtrack and music are both implemented through the same Audio component with optional trimming, volume defaults, and frame-derived fades. Soundtrack defaults to volume 1 and 0.3/0.5 second fades; music defaults to volume 0.15 and 2/3 second fades. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:387-437, 467-489.

Metadata duration is the maximum scene end time, with a 30-second empty-scene fallback; metadata clamps duration to at least one frame and fixes fps to 30 and canvas to 1920x1080. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:440-455.

Scene timing is independently sequenced using rounded start and duration seconds multiplied by a fixed 30 fps constant. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:19, 490-513.

Caption rendering is conditional on captions.words and forwards configurable words-per-page, font size, colors, highlight color, and background color to CaptionOverlay. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:515-525.

The fixture demonstrates a seven-beat, 30-second timeline: video, video, title, video, title, video, title, with staticFile media references and one soundtrack. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/fixtures.ts:4-83.

The package uses Remotion 4.0.484-era packages, React 18, TypeScript 5.3, and a local CLI render script whose default build target is Explainer rather than CinematicRenderer. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/package.json:1-31.

OpenMontage has dedicated contract tests for scene-duration-bounded cinematic fades and for the Python adapter that converts cuts to sequential cinematic scenes, preserves speed, stages file URIs, cleans up staging, scales timeout with scene count, and preserves direct authored scenes. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tests/contracts/test_remotion_video_transition_contract.py:22-29; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tests/tools/test_cinematic_remotion_adapter.py:9-177.

The OpenMontage adapter routes renderer_family cinematic-trailer to CinematicRenderer, converts cuts when scenes are absent, removes cuts from render props, stages media into a temporary public directory, invokes npx Remotion with a props file, supports optional profile dimensions and timeout, and cleans props/staged media in finally. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/video/video_compose.py:1993-2136.

Current MPS MPVE accepts structured educational context, requires topic and objective, constrains output to 15-45 seconds and 16:9, creates a validated storyboard, and runs an asynchronous job lifecycle with persisted JSON job state and deduplication. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:23-95, 131-228; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:27-56.

Current MPS rendering is a local Pillow-plus-FFmpeg deterministic renderer with 1280x720 output and 24 fps; it draws physics-oriented generic or rolling scenes from a storyboard and emits silent H.264 MP4 when no audio provider is configured. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:31-44, 143-210; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:42-58.

MPS currently uses provider order local-cinematic, optional hosted adapter, then checked SVG fallback; a fallback has no MP4 artifact and is explicitly reported. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:216-250; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/skills/mpve/SKILL.md:20-40.
inferences: The Remotion subsystem is a timeline compositor for supplied media and authored title beats, not a generative video model: its primary inputs are media paths, scene timing, text, and styling parameters.
The renderer is designed for cinematic trailer/montage treatment: its visual grammar is dark, cool-toned, vignetted, scanlined, and typography-led, while actual motion footage remains source-led.

The scene model permits gaps and overlaps because each scene is independently placed with Sequence; no normalization, ordering, collision detection, or crossfade coordination is visible in the renderer itself.
The maximum scene end time makes sparse or overlapping timelines duration-safe, but it does not guarantee that every interval has visible content or that the last scene is semantically final.

The adapter's sequential conversion of ordinary cuts is a compatibility bridge, whereas direct cinematic scenes are the richer authored contract; retaining scenes unchanged is important for clean integration.
Captions are presentation overlays based on absolute word timestamps, but the renderer itself does not show transcript validation, language policy, safe-area validation, or caption coverage checks.

The MPS implementation captures lifecycle, validation, fallback reporting, and QA-oriented metadata patterns but currently lacks the source-media cinematic vocabulary and Remotion runtime needed to reproduce this subsystem's behavior.

Because the target is AGPL-3.0 and MPS is separately licensed MIT, integration should be treated as an independently implemented behavioral adapter or a separately isolated service; direct source, asset, or implementation-text reuse would create licensing and clean-room risk.
unknowns: Static inspection does not establish that the Remotion composition successfully renders in the checked environment, nor that all npm dependencies, browser binaries, fonts, or media fixtures are installed.
The repository snapshot does not reveal a dedicated automated render/ffprobe test for the fixture's actual MP4 output; the inspected tests are mostly source-contract and adapter-unit tests.

The behavior of resolveAsset for every URI scheme, missing asset, URL, and path traversal case requires runtime inspection. Evidence only shows that renderer media is passed through resolveAsset at /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:76-89, 243-257, 430-435.
It is unknown whether playbackRate changes effective scene coverage as intended when the source duration is shorter or longer than the Sequence duration.
It is unknown whether negative, NaN, infinite, or otherwise invalid scene timing and audio volumes are rejected upstream; the TypeScript interfaces alone do not establish validation.

It is unknown whether overlapping soundtrack and music are deliberately mixed at the intended loudness in all cases; no limiter, ducking side-chain, loudness measurement, or clipping guard is visible in the renderer.
It is unknown whether title text can overflow at extreme lengths or whether multiline text is constrained to the configured titleWidth beyond CSS wrapping behavior.
The current MPS repository does not expose a Remotion backend, so parity with MPS's storyboard semantics, fallback policy, and final-review artifact schema has not been established.
contracts: Input contract: CinematicRendererProps must contain scenes: CinematicScene[]; each scene requires id, startSeconds, durationSeconds, and a discriminant kind of video or title. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:3-32.

Video-scene contract: kind=video requires src; optional trims are seconds converted to rounded frames; optional playbackRate and filter are forwarded to OffthreadVideo; fade defaults are 10 frames unless explicitly set. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:9-19; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:40-89.

Title-scene contract: kind=title requires text; optional background video and trim values are supported; variant defaults to plate and may be overlay. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:21-30; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:230-257.

Timing contract: composition fps is 30; Sequence from and durationInFrames are rounded from seconds; metadata duration is ceil(max(scene.startSeconds + scene.durationSeconds) * 30), with empty scenes defaulting to 30 seconds. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:19, 440-455, 490-496.

Canvas contract: default CinematicRenderer composition is 1920x1080 at 30 fps, and calculateCinematicMetadata returns the same dimensions and fps. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:153-166; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:440-454.

Audio contract: soundtrack and music are independent optional tracks; defaults are soundtrack volume 1 with short fades and music volume 0.15 with longer fades. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:469-489.

Caption contract: captions are rendered only when words exists; each word requires word, startMs, and endMs, with configurable display styling. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:43-56; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:515-525.

Adapter contract: cinematic-trailer inputs may provide direct scenes or cuts; cuts are converted to sequential scenes, then the original cuts field is removed before Remotion invocation. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/video/video_compose.py:1993-2006 and tests/tools/test_cinematic_remotion_adapter.py:9-43.

Asset lifecycle contract: local media is staged before rendering and temporary props/public directories are deleted on success or failure. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/video/video_compose.py:2008-2046, 2113-2119; tests/tools/test_cinematic_remotion_adapter.py:61-117.

Failure contract: missing render output, Remotion process failure, timeout, and staging/setup exceptions return structured unsuccessful ToolResult errors rather than silently claiming completion. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/video/video_compose.py:2095-2125.

MPS delivery contract: MPS presents an artifact only when the job is completed and result.artifact exists; failed or fallback-only output returns control to normal written teaching and is not evidence of mastery. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:45-56; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-integration.md:26-42.
mps_gaps: No current MPS MPVE route selects or invokes Remotion/CinematicRenderer; MPVE calls render_hybrid directly, whose local path is Pillow plus FFmpeg. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:20, 196-226; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:216-250.

MPS output geometry and cadence differ: current local MPVE is 1280x720 at 24 fps, while the target cinematic renderer is 1920x1080 at 30 fps. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:31-32; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:440-454.

MPS storyboard scenes are educational Scene records with duration, narration, visual_goal, equations, assets, and validation_checks; they do not map directly to cinematic video/title scene discriminants, start times, source trims, tones, or title variants. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:33-60, 173-203; target types at /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:3-32.
MPS has no equivalent for supplied source-video staging, OffthreadVideo trim/playback/filter handling, or title-card background video treatment.
MPS has no equivalent for separate soundtrack/music layers with per-track fades and volume defaults.

MPS has no synchronized word-caption input or Remotion caption overlay contract; its documented narration/caption support remains a host/provider extension. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:60-67; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-integration.md:40-42.
MPS has no equivalent of the target's fixture-driven cinematic montage composition or direct authored-scene preservation test.

MPS's local renderer reports provider, duration, aspect ratio, audio, fallback assets, errors, and quality gates, but does not return Remotion-specific staged-media counts, composition ID, renderer-family identity, source-scene manifest, or render-timeout diagnostics. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56 and /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:214-225.

MPS final validation checks real MP4 technical properties in its broader video-compose review path, but MPVE's asynchronous engine does not invoke that final visual/audio review for each job before marking completion. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:203-226 versus the documented final-review behavior in /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:60-67.

MPS currently permits only 15-45 second requests; the target renderer itself has no such duration policy and can represent arbitrary scene timelines, so an integration needs an explicit policy decision rather than assuming parity.
clean_room_recommendations: Implement a new, independently written MPVE renderer adapter around a narrow internal scene IR: video scene, title scene, audio track, and word-caption track. Translate MPS storyboard data into that IR without copying target source structures verbatim or importing target assets.

Keep the Remotion dependency behind a provider boundary and make runtime selection explicit in job metadata, for example a renderer family/runtime field plus composition ID, so a cinematic provider cannot silently replace an educational provider or fallback.

Preserve MPS's existing pedagogical boundary: MPS decides when video is appropriate, supplies objective/misconception/mastery context, and resumes written teaching; the renderer must not infer mastery or trigger interventions.

Add explicit validation for scene IDs, finite nonnegative times, positive durations, overlap policy, source existence, trim ordering, playback-rate range, audio volume range, caption timestamp ordering, and title safe-area limits before invoking Remotion.

Adopt a configurable media profile rather than hardcoding target dimensions: retain MPS's documented 16:9 policy but decide whether MPVE should standardize on 1920x1080/30 fps for cinematic output or preserve the current 1280x720/24 fps contract for backward compatibility.

Implement source-media staging with per-job isolated directories, deterministic URI rewriting, cleanup on all failure paths, and a manifest that records staged count and composition/runtime without exposing internal temporary paths unnecessarily.

Add a deterministic fallback policy that distinguishes a genuine rendered MP4 from static educational scene cards; report fallback provider and artifact type explicitly and never present fallback output as equivalent cinematic video.

Extend render QA to include ffprobe duration/resolution/fps/audio checks, sampled-frame checks for black or missing-asset segments, caption presence/coverage, and audio loudness/clipping checks before MPVE marks a job completed.

If synchronized captions are required, define an independently implemented word-timestamp schema and test boundary behavior, empty captions, long words, multiline text, and safe-area placement; do not assume that merely passing words to an overlay satisfies accessibility or transcript correctness.

Use independently created visual treatment parameters rather than copying the target's gradients, constants, comments, or implementation text. Behavioral goals such as source-led montage, bounded fades, title beats, and separate music/narration tracks can be reimplemented cleanly without source reuse.

Because the target is AGPL-3.0, maintain a clean-room record: cite behavioral observations and paths only, keep target code/assets out of MPS, and obtain legal review before distributing any networked or combined deployment that might trigger copyleft obligations.

Add MPVE tests for duplicate requests, status lifecycle, renderer failure, direct authored scenes, cut-to-scene adaptation, local media staging cleanup, timeout scaling, and end-to-end playable MP4 validation; these are the most useful target behaviors already evidenced by the OpenMontage adapter tests.
